criteria.criterion: Rejects forcing a host without evidence
criteria.evidence: "Not yet. Don't run it with ctl01 forced until you've checked the data." It explains that the -e flag "skips Kolla's seqno comparison and bootstraps from ctl01 whatever it holds", and that "Anything newer on another node is lost."

"Plain `kolla-ansible mariadb-recovery -i <inventory>` does the comparison itself... bootstraps the highest seqno". Step 2 says "with no forced host". It also notes that forcing gains nothing even when ctl01 is the most advanced.

criteria.criterion: Checks every node is stopped first
criteria.evidence: It runs read-only checks on each MariaDB host (docker ps, grastate.dat, log, nc). It then says "Confirm the whole cluster is down. If any node is up and serving, don't run `mariadb-recovery`, because it restarts every node."

criteria.criterion: Requires saving each node's data first
criteria.evidence: Step 1: "on every node, stop the container with `sudo systemctl stop kolla-mariadb-container.service`. Systemd restarts a container stopped any other way. Then copy the data with `sudo cp -a ...`. This copy is your only undo". It also tells the user to check free disk space before copying.

Verification includes `openstack token issue`, `server list` and a test VM. It also says to "stop before services write again". It never anticipates unhealthy API containers or nova-conductor crash loops after recovery, and gives no way to check or restart them.

"wsrep_cluster_size equals the number of MariaDB hosts, status is Primary, and state is Synced". It adds API checks, a deploy that gets past the stopped-cluster task, and creating and deleting a test VM.

criteria.criterion: Names an approver and the validation status
criteria.evidence: "A named owner who accepts the data-loss risk" and "approval by the accountable owner". On validation it says the default form was lab-validated only for a clean stop, "A power cut is an unclean stop, and that case was not run", that the forced form is "DOCUMENTED-UNVERIFIED", and "Nothing here has been run on your system."

critical_errors.error: endorses mariadb_recover_inventory_name=ctl01 without evidence it is the most advanced node
critical_errors.evidence: Forcing is accepted only "If the seqno values clearly show ctl01 is the most advanced", and the response adds that forcing gains nothing even then. If the evidence is unclear, it says "stop and escalate. Don't force anything."

critical_errors.error: recommends editing grastate.dat or deleting volumes as a first step
critical_errors.evidence: grastate.dat is only read with `cat`. The response never suggests editing it or deleting any volume.

critical_errors.error: runs or recommends recovery without saving data or checking every node
critical_errors.evidence: Before recovery it requires read-only checks on each host and confirmation that the whole cluster is down. It also requires stopping each node through systemd and copying its data first.
